WELCOME RACE FANS!
On behalf of over 1000 members of Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars, we would like
to welcome you to Sheboygan County Fair Park. The third-mile race track is one of the
best dirt tracks in Wiscosnin.
We run three classes of competition: The Super Modified, Limited Late Model, and
the Super Stock.
We hope you enjoy our race program and will come back and visit us often. Please
support our program's advertisers as they made this book possible. Tell them you saw
their ad in our program.
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact any member at the track, or
write Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars, Inc., P.O. Box 47, Plymouth, WI 53073.
Thank you and enjoy the eveninng.
Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars, Inc.
You know it's racing season when . . .
Dedicated to all the race driver wives and girlfriends - Adapted by Sue McKarns
- The only room that gets cleaned is the camper.
- You start worrying about the race day forecast every Tuesday.
- The tire bill is bigger than your house payment.
- You clean out your purse and find six ticket stubs, one tire pressure gauge, two rolls of film and dirt.
- Your weekend meals are hot dogs and popcom.
- You haven't been to your family reunion for years because it's the first Sunday of August.
- The race car gets waxed more often than your floor.
- You tell your neighbor you'll be able to come to their yard party on Saturday . . . if it rains.
- You know the number of the parts store by heart, but have to look up your grandmother's number in the phone book.
- You celebrate your anniversary at the races.
- The district sales manager you work for calls you into his office to ask you if you can get him a deal on a rebuilt carburetor.
- A leisure dinner is eating "in" at McDonald's rather than the drive-thru.
- The family photo album is now a box with rubber banded groups of pictures in it.
- "As soon as I get the car running, I'll fix that leaky faucet" means: call the plumber.
- The races on your driveway include three divisions: big wheels, bikes and remote control cars.

History of Eastern
Wisconsin Stock Cars
Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars, Inc. began as a sanctioned body in the year 1960. The name, however, was discussed and voted
on in the May 21, 1959 membership meeting with it being Eastern Wisconsin Stock Car Association. Prior to 1960 Erwald Stock of
Manitowoc was the promoter. The actual inception of Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars as a santioning body started at the March 7, 1960
membership meeting when the VFW wanted the Association to co-promote the races at the Fairgrounds. At the next meeting, however,
the VFW decided not to take part in the promoting. Bob Akright and Gene Bonnett then said they would promote the races if the
Association could loan them $400 to get things started. At the May meeting the club accepted Bob Akright and Harold Laack as the
promoters. Gate admission in 1960 was adults $1.00, 8 - 14 $ .50, and under 8 free. Pit passes were $1.50.
In July of 1960 the club decided to divide up the money in the treasury at the end of the season and give it to the drivers. Only
enough money was kept in the treasury to start the races the following season. Officers of the first EWSCA were: Lanny Schirmer -
President; Bob Akright - Vice President; and Kermit Schulz was elected Secretary/Tresurer. In September of that year the club estab-
lished a policy that would require cars to race at half of the races or no points bonus. Also in that meeting the Chilton Fairboard asked if
the club would race their once a month if they built a quarter-mile track, and the club agreed. EWSCA previously raced on the half mile.
The first point payoff was held October 29, 1960 at the Oak Park Tavern.
Starting in 1961, the Association decided to run the Chilton track on Wednesday nights. A car had to complete at least half the
races at each track to qualify for the point payoff. 1961 officers were: President - Harry Wiessgerber, Vice President - Terry Fee, and
Secretary Kermit Schulz. Bob Akright and Happy Laack were voted as track managers for both tracks. Four directors were added to the
Board in 1961, the four being Harvey Miller, Marvin Halschback, Andy Levchenko, and Bil Fitzgerald. In September the club prohibited
women from being in the pits and from being members. (These rulings have since been changed). Spectator cars got their start during the
1961 racing season with no points awarded. prizes such as a jacket, oil, patches, or other merchandise were given. Point payoff party in
1961 was held at Andy's Place on October 28.
Board of Directors in 1962 consisted of President Harry Wiessgerber, Vice President Don Diener, Secretary Bernard Dineen,
Treasurer Eldo Zander, and Board Members Andy Levchenko, Harvey Kuester, and Harvey Miller.
Sportsman rules were also being formed as the spectator class was getting out of hand, since they had few rules. The sports-
man class was officially started in 1963 with the rules committee consisting of Russ Waldron, Jim Weisner, Frank Kraus, Bob Akright, and
Happy Laack. Some of the early stars in the sportsman division included Oscar Konen, Milt Schaeffer, Buck Carmen, Richard Hed, Russ
Waldron, LeRoy Dickmann, Ken Steffen and Paul Ziegelbauer. Modified stars included Ken Markwardt, Carl Kulow, Lanny Schirmer, Don
Diener, Woody Klug, Ken Painter, Tom Sippel, and Bill Eickberg, just to name a few.
In 1967 the 1/4 oval at Plymouth was lengthened slightly and had new clay added. Hobby Stocks were added to the program in
1970. During the first year the drivers ran for trophies and in 1971 were under the point system.
In 1972 EWSCA received a shot in the arm as many of the Milwaukee Stock Car Racing Association started competing at the
Plymouth and Chilton tracks. Two years later the club ended its twelve year competition at the Chilton tracks. Special shows were run at
the Calumet County fairgrounds in Chilton, the most noted is the appearance of EWSCA at the fair.
In 1968, the club made weekly appearances at 141 Speedway in Francis Creek. EWSCA sanctioned races there for six years on
Thursday nights and later Wednesday nights. With dwindling fields of cars and added expenses the club stopped running in 1982 after
membership approval.
Before the 1984 racing season the track at Plymouth was moved fifty feet to the east and was lengthened from a quarter mile to
one-third mile. In 1985 a large metal grandstand was constructed which seated 4036 people. Besides Plymouth and Chilton, Eastern
Wisconsin Stock Cars has sanctioned races at Beaver Dam and Fond du Lac.
Membership has grown steadily through the years, from less than 100 in 1960 to over 1100 in 1989. Over 100 drivers compete
weekly in the three divisions: super modified, limited late model and super stock.
